profile_md: UNSW has a centrally run, term-based experiential learning course, CDEV3000/CDEV6000 Practice of Work (6 UOC), in which students from different degrees work in interdisciplinary teams on a brief set by an external industry, community or government partner. Summer Term 2027 and Term 1 2027 offerings are listed, so this is the best-evidenced route. Distributed beneath it are faculty routes: the School of Computer Science and Engineering Industry Capstone Program (teams of 6, external client supervises over a 10-week term, 2026 flyer), the Science Industry Project SCIF3000 (multidisciplinary teams, live partner project, WAM 65+ and 60 UOC; page undated), and in the Business School COMM2233 Industry Consulting Project (small teams at a host organisation, 2024-dated evidence) and short virtual Business Experience Projects (about 25 hours over 2 weeks). Participation is elective or selective in each case; no university-wide compulsory route was found. The legacy COMM1120 core course could not be tested because the handbook page carries no description. AHEGS Advantage is a recognition framework, not a project route. Uncertain: current delivery of SCIF3000, COMM2233 and Business Experience Projects; degree-level eligibility for CDEV; compulsory status and codes of the CSE capstones; Arts/Social Sciences and Law team-project routes.
gaps: Reduced-depth run (about 8 searches plus 8 page fetches). Not opened: Business postgraduate practicum courses, Chemical Engineering/Industrial Design capstones, VIPs, ADA Innovation Hub, Law Social Impact Hub, Medicine. Further departmental instances are likely. COMM1120/COMM3900 handbook descriptions unavailable (pages note newer versions exist). Fetch tool summarises pages, so quotes are partly paraphrased.
